body.statement: For every fixed \(K\), every \(c\in\mathcal C_K\), every outcome-independent possibly dependent design \(\mathcal D_n\), and every possibly randomized full-label estimator \(\widehat\tau\), \[\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}\mathcal R_n(\mathcal D_n,\widehat\tau;y)\ge n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),\] where the remainder is uniform over the design-estimator pair. Equivalently, \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)\le\Lambda_c\).
body.justification: The lower theorem turns a fixed-design Airy expansion into an unrestricted joint design-estimation result.
body.gap: Bai (2023), Theorem 2.1, supplies permutation symmetrization; Theorem 3.1 reduces the minimax problem over linear-estimator schemes to minimization of a quadratic expected form subject to linear constraints over assignment and estimator schemes; and Theorem 3.2 gives the two-arm complete-randomization, Neyman-allocation, and difference-in-means specialization. These results do not control arbitrary binary schedules, nonlinear estimators, or the second-order coefficient.
body.consumer: The theorem rules out correlated or face-supported randomizations that could otherwise invalidate the proposed clinical allocation.
